answer: In an AI-agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each identity to sustain a living trellis of multi-epoch peer attestations tied to original work. An attacker who wants many fake agents must fund a continuous voyage of unique quill-written answers and ongoing compute for every identity across epochs; that cumulative cost of time, capital, and originality grows faster than the linear reward of any single fake, making large-scale identity farming uneconomic.
